scope: Sandbox changes offered to the Stu/loop owner, not general collector instructions.
claims: Fork batching mode1 matches its mode2 reference, but changes main draws versus old mode0. NumPy feature scatter and legal-suit-only policy have sandbox checks; matrix-size/kernel differences need real-host comparisons. Gen8 sg8 profile is Stu's self-play, not this arena cohort; bf16 has no claimed card equivalence.
disposition: Retain frozen792c4cb FP32 source, existing seeds/streams, DDS semantics and scientific identity. Do not set new BRIDGE_* switches, add torch/BF16, benchmark peer boxes, alter own source, self-play or BEN.

perf: legal-suit decoding test at the real net's sizes (bit-identical) and within 1e-5 at tiny sizes; README items 4 and Gen 8 profile

gen7_net: policy logits decode only the suits holding a legal card (forward_policy, Bf16Forward.policy)

log_policy_arrays needs only the legal cards' policy logits. 55% of rollout rows follow
suit, so most suit decodings and four of five output columns are skipped. The legal
cards' log-probabilities are identical to the full pass (tests/test_bf16_buckets.py);
forward pass +5-15% fp32, +0-12% bf16 in the sandbox, end to end within noise there.
BRIDGE_POLICY_SUITS=0 turns it off. README: Gen 8 self-play profile.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N2EvxFxonBEZD9BNLUssr4

gen7_net: NumPy features written into one array with a scatter (same numbers, about 2.5x faster)

features() was 9% of a bf16 self-play table. The NumPy path now scatters the state
one-hot and writes the other per-card features in place instead of a [n, 52, 11]
comparison and a six-way concatenation: identical arrays (tests/test_bf16_buckets.py),
1.66 to 0.71 ms at 512 rows, about 7% of a table in the sandbox. JAX keeps the generic
path; BRIDGE_FAST_FEATURES=0 restores it for NumPy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N2EvxFxonBEZD9BNLUssr4

8X rollouts: fork continuations ride in the main rows' batches (x8_rollout.FORK_BATCH)

The fork copies were finished after the main loop one group at a time, two rows a
net call: half of all net calls and about 10% of a self-play table. From the step a
fork is taken its copies are at the main rows' ply, so they now advance in the same
net evaluation (Seats.cards_pair), drawing from their own stream so the main rows'
draws do not depend on them. Sandbox, 6 boards: fp32 20.3 to 18.3 CPU-s a board,
padded bf16 12.6 to 9.4, the same cards as the old path on the fork stream (mode 2).
Against the old path on the main stream (BRIDGE_FORK_BATCH=0) the draws after a race's
first round differ: same distribution, not the same cards.
